title: Inference Fidelity vs Throughput Allocator - Scenario Lab Notes
content:
Purpose:
Short lab-style worksheet to capture tradeoffs between inference fidelity (quality) and throughput/cost across GPU families, quantization profiles, and batching configurations. This is an exploratory artifact for infra + applied-ml to pick candidate configs for the Q2 dedicated capacity pilot.

Summary findings (high level):
- Small/medium sequences (<=512) are throughput-sensitive: 4-bit quant + batching gives ~3.6x throughput uplift with ~1.8% relative quality delta on summary ROUGE-L in our synthetic eval.
- Large sequences (>=2048) show diminishing batching returns due to KV cache overhead; 8-bit config keeps latency more predictable.
- A hybrid router that prefers q4_0 for short requests and q8_0 fallback for long ones reduces tail latency violations by ~22% while preserving ~98.5% of baseline quality.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline model: open-llm-13b (FP16) tuned on retrieval-augmented summarization tasks. Baseline metrics collected on A100-40GB.
- Quality metric: primary = ROUGE-L (document summarization); secondary = human acceptance rate proxy (binary automated classifier tuned against small human label set).
- Cost proxy: token-GPU-second converted to $ using committed price model: A100-40: $3.2/hr; H100-80: $6.4/hr; L4: $1.1/hr (for on-demand rough math).
- Workload mix: 70% short chat/summary (avg seq 256 tokens), 20% medium (512-1024), 10% long (>2048).
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 450ms for short, <=900ms medium, <=1500ms long. Utilization target 65-75% to leave headroom for bursts.

Scenario table (simulated):
Columns: Scenario | Model Variant | Quant | Batch | GPU | Avg Seq | Expected RPS | p95 Latency(ms) | Cost per 1M tokens ($) | Quality delta vs FP16 (ROUGE-L pct) | Notes
1) Short-optimised | open-llm-13b | q4_0 | 16 | L4 | 256 | 3200 | 380 | 28.5 | -1.8% | aggressive batching; high throughput, watch tail
2) Balanced | open-llm-13b | q8_0 | 8 | A100-40 | 512 | 1200 | 430 | 40.1 | -0.6% | good balance, predictable latencies
3) Long-safe | open-llm-13b | q8_0 | 4 | H100-80 | 2048 | 180 | 720 | 75.3 | -0.2% | prioritize quality for long sequences
4) Mixed-hybrid-router | open-llm-13b | q4_0/q8_0 | dynamic | fleet (L4+A100) | mix | 2100 | 470 | 33.7 | -1.1% | router chooses q4_0 for <512 seq, q8_0 otherwise
5) Conservative | open-llm-13b | fp16 | 2 | A100-40 | mix | 600 | 520 | 120.9 | 0.0% | baseline; lowest quality delta

Notes on numbers:
- Expected RPS and p95 were derived from microbench harness with realistic request jitter and synthetic KV cache warmup curves. Absolute numbers are lab estimates for planning only.
- Cost per 1M tokens is a simple conversion using token length * avg model throughput * GPU hourly price normalized; does not include infra overhead (network, control plane).

Sensitivity analysis snapshots (what to vary next):
- Sensitivity to mix shift: if short requests drop from 70% to 40%, hybrid router loses ~12% throughput; A100-backed q8_0 config becomes more cost-efficient.
- Sensitivity to cache hit rate: if KV cache hit rate falls from 80% to 50% for long seqs, p95 for long-safe scenario increases ~18%.
- Quality threshold cliff: automated eval shows a non-linear drop in human acceptance once ROUGE-L delta exceeds ~2.5% (classifier calibrated). Keep safety margin <=2% for user-facing features.

Operational considerations:
- Autoscaling granularity: batching gains are time-window sensitive; if autoscaler scales down too aggressively we lose batching-efficiency. Recommend minimum stable batch window of 250ms for short-path pools.
- Rollout strategy: A/B test with traffic shaping (5% -> 20% -> 50%) and continuous quality-eval on golden prompt set. Gate rollback on acceptance rate drop >1.5% or p95 violation >10% over baseline.
- Fallbacks: implement model-variant fallback (q4_0 -> q8_0 -> fp16) in routing policy with per-route counters and cooldown to avoid mass fallbacks.

Open questions / tradeoffs to decide:
- Acceptable quality delta per product vertical (search vs summaries vs code generation). Research suggests codegen tolerates lower ROUGE-like metrics but needs semantic correctness checks.
- Should we standardize on single quant profile per fleet or allow per-route quantization? (Operational complexity vs cost win).
- Do we reserve a small fp16 pool for high-value customers / regulatory workloads? What is minimal reserve size to keep p95 SLAs?

Next steps / action items:
- Applied ML: produce a short 25-sample human eval comparing q4_0 vs q8_0 vs fp16 for the top 3 customer prompt templates (Owner: Priya) — due 2026-03-09.
- Infra: run a 48-hr pilot on dedicated L4 pool with hybrid router enabled (Owner: Diego) — schedule week of 2026-03-15.
- SRE: add a control-plane metric for "batch-window-ms" per pool to make batching visibility first-class (Owner: Owen) — due 2026-03-19.

Appendix A: quick simulation snippets (pseudocode)
- Sim harness: simulate(requests, profile, quant, batch_size, gpu_latency_curve) -> estimated_rps, p95, token_cost
- Router policy: if seq_len < 512 and pool_util < 75% then prefer q4_0 pool else route to q8_0; backoff to fp16 on >3 consecutive p95 violations

Appendix B: raw microbench observations (examples):
- L4 q4_0 batch 16, seq 256: observed tail jitter when burst > 3x steady-state; ensure request queuing cap.
- A100 q8_0 batch 8, seq 512: steady throughput with p95 within 5% of mean; KV cache warmup required 90s for stable performance.

- Confluence: /space/INFRA/quant-batch-guidelines (draft)
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-1243 (hybrid-router design), JIRA-OPS-2107 (batching telemetry)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987 (router prototype)

Notes to self: capture more production-like prompt variety (SRE logs) before committing to Q2 capacity buys.

-- Maya
